title: pretext
description: 진짜 이유가 아닌, 겉으로 내세우는 표면적인 이유나 변명을 가리킬 때 사용합니다.
"excuse"보다 더 계획적이고 의도적인 느낌을 줄 때가 많습니다.
예: "He used the meeting as a pretext to leave early." (그는 일찍 나가기 위한 구실로 회의를 이용했다.)

conversations.title: 회사에서 일찍 퇴근할 핑계를 댈 때

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why did John leave so early today?
lines.meaning: 존이 오늘 왜 그렇게 일찍 나갔어?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He said he had a doctor’s appointment, but I think it was just a pretext to skip the afternoon meeting.
lines.meaning: 의사 예약이 있다고 했는데, 사실 오후 회의를 빼기 위한 핑계였을 거야.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you really have to work late last night?
lines.meaning: 어제 진짜 야근해야 했어?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. I used work as a pretext because I didn’t want to go to that dinner.
lines.meaning: 아니. 그 저녁 약속 가기 싫어서 일을 핑계로 댄 거야.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why did the government suddenly increase security?
lines.meaning: 정부가 갑자기 왜 보안을 강화한 거야?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They claimed it was for public safety, but many people see it as a pretext to increase surveillance.
lines.meaning: 공공 안전을 위해서라고 했지만, 많은 사람들이 감시를 늘리기 위한 명분이라고 보고 있어.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You canceled our plans again. What’s the excuse this time?
lines.meaning: 또 약속 취소했네. 이번엔 무슨 핑계야?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I said I was sick, but honestly it was just a pretext. I was too tired to go out.
lines.meaning: 아프다고 했는데, 사실 그냥 핑계였어. 너무 피곤해서 나가기 싫었어.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where’s Sarah? She’s been gone for over an hour.
lines.meaning: 사라 어디 갔어? 한 시간 넘게 안 보이네.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: She said she needed to check something with IT, but I suspect it was a pretext to take a long break.
lines.meaning: IT팀이랑 확인할 게 있다고 했는데, 사실 길게 쉬려고 한 핑계 같아.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why did he suddenly break up with her?
lines.meaning: 걔가 갑자기 왜 헤어졌어?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He said they wanted different things, but everyone knows that was just a pretext.
lines.meaning: 서로 원하는 게 다르다고 했지만, 다들 그게 그냥 핑계라는 거 알고 있어.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Was the border dispute the real reason for the conflict?
lines.meaning: 국경 분쟁이 진짜 분쟁 원인이었어?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not really. It was mostly used as a pretext to justify the invasion.
lines.meaning: 사실 아니야. 침공을 정당화하기 위한 명분으로 주로 쓰였지.

conversations.title: 가족 사이에서 거짓 이유를 댈 때

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mom said she can’t come because she’s busy with work.
lines.meaning: 엄마가 일 때문에 바쁘다고 못 온대.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That’s just a pretext. She simply doesn’t want to deal with the relatives this weekend.
lines.meaning: 그건 그냥 핑계야. 이번 주말에 친척들 상대하기 싫은 거지.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you really need another pair of shoes?
lines.meaning: 신발 진짜 또 필요했어?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I told myself it was for work, but that was just a pretext. I just wanted them.
lines.meaning: 일 때문에 필요하다고 스스로 합리화했지만, 그냥 사고 싶어서 산 핑계였어.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why is the company suddenly restructuring the team?
lines.meaning: 회사가 갑자기 왜 팀 구조를 바꾸려는 거야?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They say it’s to improve efficiency, but many believe it’s a pretext to lay people off quietly.
lines.meaning: 효율성을 높이기 위해서라고 하지만, 조용히 인원을 줄이려는 명분이라고 보는 사람들이 많아.
